name: MI-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of D+9
Jeremy Moss's large fundraising advantage over Ethan Baker
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 96%
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Democrats holding this seat: a D+9 partisan lean, a favorable environment, and Jeremy Moss outraising Ethan Baker roughly ten-to-one with outside support on his side. Markets agree, pricing a Democratic win at about 96%, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin with no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Baker or a polling surprise showing single digits would be the main signals that this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Haley Stevens (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Haley Stevens is leaving this Detroit-area seat to run for Senate, making it an open-seat contest between Democrat Jeremy Moss and Republican Ethan Baker, with minor-party and independent candidates also on the ballot. The district's D+9 lean and a favorable national environment for Democrats give the party a strong structural advantage, and Moss has raised nearly $1.5 million to Baker's roughly $142,000, with outside groups adding further support on the Democratic side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic hold at about 96%. The expected margin is in the high teens, consistent with a Safe D rating, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
